# DynamoDB Data Model

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design applies aggregate-oriented principles by grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 75% of user profile queries also need recent order history, making User+Orders a natural item collection aggregate. Additionally, orders are always accessed with their items (95% correlation), making Order+OrderItems a single item aggregate. Products remain separate due to independent access patterns and scaling needs.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**User+Orders Item Collection**: Combined due to 75% access correlation, identifying relationship (orders belong to users), and bounded size (32KB max). This eliminates the need for a separate Orders table and GSI.

**Order+OrderItems Single Item**: Embedded order items as a list attribute since 95% of order access needs complete order details, updates happen atomically, and combined size stays small (6KB average).

**Products Separate**: Kept independent due to low correlation with other entities (10%), different scaling patterns (catalog growth vs user growth), and distinct operational needs (inventory management).

## Table Designs

### Users Table

| PK (user_id) | SK | name | email | addresses | order_date | order_status | order_total | order_items |
|--------------|----|----- |-------|-----------|------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | John Doe | john@email.com | [{street: "123 Main St", city: "NYC"}] | | | | |
| user_123 | ORDER#ord_456 | | | | 2024-01-15 | shipped | 89.99 | [{product_id: "prod_789", name: "Widget", quantity: 2, price: 44.99}] |
| user_123 | ORDER#ord_457 | | | | 2024-01-20 | processing | 129.99 | [{product_id: "prod_790", name: "Gadget", quantity: 1, price: 129.99}] |
| user_456 | PROFILE | Jane Smith | jane@email.com | [{street: "456 Oak Ave", city: "LA"}] | | | | |
| user_456 | ORDER#ord_458 | | | | 2024-01-18 | delivered | 199.99 | [{product_id: "prod_789", name: "Widget", quantity: 1, price: 44.99}, {product_id: "prod_791", name: "Tool", quantity: 1, price: 155.00}] |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profiles and their complete order history in a single table using item collection pattern
- **Aggregate Boundary**: User profile data and all orders belonging to that user, optimized for the 75% of queries that need both
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Provides even distribution across 1000 users, each partition handles ~0.05 RPS well within limits
- **Sort Key**: PROFILE for user data, ORDER#<order_id> for orders - Enables querying user profile alone or with order history
- **SK Taxonomy**: `PROFILE` (user profile data), `ORDER#<order_id>` (individual orders with embedded items)
- **Attributes**: name (S), email (S), addresses (L), order_date (S), order_status (S), order_total (N), order_items (L of Maps)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query with SK begins_with "ORDER#" and limit 20 for pagination, typical page size 10 orders
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #1 (user profile), #2 (create user), #3 (update user), #4 (order history), #5 (order details), #6 (place order), #7 (update order status)
- **Capacity Planning**: 120 RPS total across all user patterns, well distributed across partitions

### Products Table

| PK (product_id) | name | category | price | inventory | description | created_at |
|-----------------|------|----------|-------|-----------|-------------|------------|
| prod_789 | Premium Widget | electronics | 44.99 | 150 | High-quality widget for daily use | 2024-01-01 |
| prod_790 | Smart Gadget | electronics | 129.99 | 75 | Advanced gadget with smart features | 2024-01-02 |
| prod_791 | Professional Tool | tools | 155.00 | 200 | Professional-grade tool for experts | 2024-01-03 |
| prod_792 | Home Appliance | home | 299.99 | 50 | Essential home appliance | 2024-01-04 |
| prod_793 | Office Supply | office | 19.99 | 500 | Standard office supply item | 2024-01-05 |

- **Purpose**: Stores product catalog with inventory management, optimized for browsing and direct lookups
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Individual products with their metadata, pricing, and inventory levels
- **Partition Key**: product_id - Natural high-cardinality key providing even distribution across growing catalog
- **Sort Key**: None - Products are accessed directly by ID or through GSI for category browsing
- **Attributes**: name (S), category (S), price (N), inventory (N), description (S), created_at (S)
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #10 (product details), #11 (inventory check), #12 (inventory update), #13 (add product), #14 (update product)
- **Capacity Planning**: 190 RPS for direct product lookups, distributed across product catalog

### ProductsByCategory GSI

| GSI_PK (category) | GSI_SK (product_id) | name | price | inventory |
|-------------------|---------------------|------|-------|-----------|
| electronics | prod_789 | Premium Widget | 44.99 | 150 |
| electronics | prod_790 | Smart Gadget | 129.99 | 75 |
| tools | prod_791 | Professional Tool | 155.00 | 200 |
| home | prod_792 | Home Appliance | 299.99 | 50 |
| office | prod_793 | Office Supply | 19.99 | 500 |

- **Purpose**: Enables browsing products by category for catalog navigation and filtering
- **Partition Key**: category - Distributes products across categories, potential hot partition on popular categories like "electronics"
- **Sort Key**: product_id - Provides consistent ordering and enables pagination
- **Projection**: INCLUDE - Projects name, price, inventory attributes needed for product browsing without additional GetItem calls
- **Per‑Pattern Projected Attributes**: Pattern #8 (browse by category) needs name, price, inventory for product listings
- **Sparse**: Not applicable - All products have categories
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #8 (browse products by category)
- **Capacity Planning**: 100 RPS for category browsing, monitor for hot partitions on popular categories

## Access Pattern Mapping

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | Get user profile by user ID | Users | GetItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Direct lookup, <3ms target |
| 2 | Create new user account | Users | PutItem with condition | Use email uniqueness check |
| 3 | Update user profile | Users | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Simple attribute updates |
| 4 | List user's order history | Users | Query(user_id, SK begins_with "ORDER#") | Paginated with limit 20 |
| 5 | Get complete order details | Users | GetItem(user_id, "ORDER#<order_id>") | Single item with embedded items |
| 6 | Place new order | Users, Products | TransactWrite: PutItem + UpdateItem | Atomic order creation + inventory decrement |
| 7 | Update order status | Users | UpdateItem(user_id, "ORDER#<order_id>") | Status and timestamp updates |
| 8 | Browse products by category | ProductsByCategory GSI | Query(category) with pagination | Use GSI for category filtering |
| 9 | Search products by name | Products + OpenSearch | Scan with FilterExpression or OpenSearch | Consider OpenSearch for complex search |
| 10 | Get product details | Products | GetItem(product_id) | Direct product lookup |
| 11 | Check inventory levels | Products | GetItem(product_id) projection | Inventory attribute only |
| 12 | Update product inventory | Products | UpdateItem with ADD operation | Atomic counter for inventory |
| 13 | Add new products | Products | PutItem | Standard product creation |
| 14 | Update product details | Products | UpdateItem | Price and description updates |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **Users Table**: 120 RPS distributed across 1000 users = 0.12 RPS per partition ✅
- **Products Table**: 190 RPS distributed across growing catalog (1000+ products) = <0.2 RPS per partition ✅
- **ProductsByCategory GSI**: 100 RPS concentrated on popular categories - **Potential Risk**
  - **Mitigation**: Monitor category distribution, consider write sharding for viral products if needed

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined Users+Orders due to 75% access correlation - trades operational coupling for query performance and cost savings
- **Single Item Aggregate**: Embedded OrderItems in Orders due to 95% joint access - trades item size for atomic updates and single-query retrieval
- **Denormalization**: Duplicated product name in order items to avoid lookups during order display - trades storage for read performance
- **GSI Projection**: Used INCLUDE projection on ProductsByCategory to balance cost vs performance for browsing patterns
- **Search Strategy**: Basic FilterExpression for simple name searches, recommend OpenSearch integration for complex full-text search
- **Identifying Relationship**: Used user_id as partition key for orders to eliminate separate Orders table and GSI - 50% cost reduction

Based on this comprehensive guide, here's my structured approach to DynamoDB schema design:

## My DynamoDB Design Approach

I follow a **2-phase workflow** that prioritizes understanding your business needs before diving into technical implementation:

### Phase 1: Requirements Gathering & Analysis
I start by understanding your application deeply:

1. **Application Context**: What domain you're working in, expected scale, and key business rules
2. **Access Pattern Discovery**: Every read AND write operation your application needs, with realistic RPS estimates
3. **Entity Relationship Mapping**: How your data connects and which pieces are accessed together
4. **Aggregate Analysis**: Identifying which data should be grouped together based on access patterns (not just entity relationships)

### Phase 2: Aggregate-Oriented Design
Rather than starting with "one table per entity," I design around **aggregates** - groups of data that are accessed together:

1. **Item Collection Aggregates**: Related entities sharing a partition key but as separate items (like User + Orders)
2. **Single Item Aggregates**: Multiple entities combined into one item for atomic access (like Order + OrderItems)
3. **Strategic Table Consolidation**: Eliminating unnecessary GSIs through identifying relationships

### Key Design Principles I Apply

- **Access Pattern Driven**: Your query needs determine the structure, not entity boundaries
- **Cost Optimization**: Minimize GSIs through smart partition key design and identifying relationships  
- **Hot Partition Prevention**: Ensure even load distribution across partition keys
- **Operational Simplicity**: Avoid complex single-table patterns that create maintenance overhead

### What Makes This Different

Instead of forcing everything into one table or blindly creating separate tables per entity, I analyze your **access correlation patterns**:
- >70% accessed together → Consider single item aggregate
- 30-70% accessed together → Item collection aggregate  
- <30% accessed together → Separate tables/aggregates

# DynamoDB Data Model

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design follows aggregate-oriented principles, grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 60% of user profile requests also need recent order history, making User+Orders a natural item collection aggregate. Orders and OrderItems are combined into single items due to 95% joint access correlation and atomic operation benefits. Products remain separate due to independent access patterns and catalog management needs.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**UserOrders Aggregate**: Combines users and their orders in an item collection due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship. This eliminates the need for a separate Orders table and GSI, reducing costs by 50%.

**Order+OrderItems Single Item Aggregate**: Embeds order items within order records due to 95% joint access and bounded size (max 25KB). Enables atomic order operations and single-read retrieval.

**Products Separate Aggregate**: Maintains independence due to distinct access patterns (browsing, searching, catalog management) and different operational characteristics.

## Table Designs

### UserOrders Table

| PK (user_id) | SK | name | email | address | order_date | total_amount | status | items |
|--------------|----|----- |-------|---------|------------|--------------|--------|-------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | John Doe | john@email.com | 123 Main St | | | | |
| user_123 | ORDER#2024-001 | | | | 2024-07-15T10:30:00Z | 89.99 | shipped | [embedded items array] |
| user_123 | ORDER#2024-002 | | | | 2024-07-20T14:15:00Z | 156.50 | processing | [embedded items array] |
| user_456 | PROFILE | Jane Smith | jane@email.com | 456 Oak Ave | | | | |
| user_456 | ORDER#2024-003 | | | | 2024-07-18T09:45:00Z | 234.75 | delivered | [embedded items array] |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profiles and their complete order history in a single table optimized for joint access patterns
- **Aggregate Boundary**: User profile data and all orders belonging to that user, leveraging the identifying relationship
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Ensures even distribution across 1000 users (~0.01 RPS per partition), natural lookup key for user operations
- **Sort Key**: PROFILE for user data, ORDER#{order_id} for orders - Enables querying user profile alone or with order history
- **SK Taxonomy**: `PROFILE` (user profile data), `ORDER#{order_id}` (individual orders with embedded items)
- **Attributes**: User: name, email, address, created_at; Order: order_date, total_amount, status, items (list of maps with product_id, product_name, quantity, price)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query with SK begins_with "ORDER#" and limit for pagination; typical page size 10 orders
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #1 (user profile), #2 (create user), #3 (update user), #4 (order history), #5 (order details), #6 (create order), #7 (update order status)
- **Capacity Planning**: 25 RPS reads, 6 RPS writes; on-demand mode suitable for this scale

| PK (product_id) | name | description | price | category | inventory | created_at |
|-----------------|------|-------------|-------|----------|-----------|------------|

| prod_005 | Bluetooth Speaker | Portable waterproof speaker | 59.99 | electronics | 34 | 2024-03-10T11:45:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Product catalog with inventory management, optimized for individual product lookups and category browsing
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Individual products with their metadata and inventory levels
- **Partition Key**: product_id - Natural identifier for product operations, ensures even distribution
- **Sort Key**: None - Simple key-value lookup pattern for individual products
- **Attributes**: name (string), description (string), price (number), category (string), inventory (number), created_at (string)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Direct GetItem for individual products; GSI queries for category browsing with pagination
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #10 (product details), #11 (inventory check), #12 (inventory update), #13 (add product), #14 (update product)
- **Capacity Planning**: 35 RPS reads, 5 RPS writes; on-demand mode

### ProductsByCategory GSI

| GSI_PK (category) | GSI_SK (product_id) | name | price | inventory |
|-------------------|---------------------|------|-------|-----------|
| electronics | prod_001 | Wireless Headphones | 199.99 | 45 |
| electronics | prod_005 | Bluetooth Speaker | 59.99 | 34 |
| sports | prod_002 | Running Shoes | 89.99 | 23 |
| sports | prod_004 | Yoga Mat | 29.99 | 67 |
| home | prod_003 | Coffee Maker | 79.99 | 12 |

- **Purpose**: Enables browsing products by category with efficient pagination and filtering
- **Partition Key**: category - Groups products by category for browsing, ~10 categories expected
- **Sort Key**: product_id - Provides consistent ordering and enables pagination
- **Projection**: INCLUDE - Projects name, price, inventory for category browsing without additional GetItem calls
- **Per‑Pattern Projected Attributes**: Pattern #8 (category browsing) needs name, price, inventory; Pattern #9 (search) uses this as fallback
- **Sparse**: Not applicable - all products have categories
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #8 (browse by category), partial support for Pattern #9 (product search)
- **Capacity Planning**: 20 RPS reads; categories well-distributed to avoid hot partitions

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | Get user profile by user ID | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Direct lookup, <3ms target |
| 2 | Create new user account | UserOrders | PutItem with condition | Use condition to prevent overwrites |
| 3 | Update user profile | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Standard update operation |
| 4 | List user's order history | UserOrders | Query(user_id) SK begins_with "ORDER#" | Pagination with limit, chronological order |
| 5 | Get complete order details | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "ORDER#{order_id}") | Single item retrieval with embedded items |
| 6 | Place new order | UserOrders | PutItem + Products UpdateItem | Transaction for inventory decrement |
| 7 | Update order status | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "ORDER#{order_id}") | Status field update |
| 8 | Browse products by category | ProductsByCategory GSI | Query(category) with pagination | Use GSI for efficient category browsing |
| 9 | Search products by name | Products + ProductsByCategory | Scan with FilterExpression | Consider OpenSearch for advanced search |
| 10 | Get product details | Products | GetItem(product_id) | Direct lookup, <2ms target |
| 11 | Check inventory levels | Products | GetItem(product_id) or BatchGetItem | Single or batch operations |
| 12 | Update product inventory | Products | UpdateItem with ADD/SET | Atomic increment/decrement operations |
| 13 | Add new products | Products | PutItem | Standard item creation |
| 14 | Update product details | Products | UpdateItem | Standard attribute updates |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **UserOrders**: Pattern #1 at 10 RPS distributed across 1000 users = 0.01 RPS per partition ✅
- **Products**: Pattern #10 at 25 RPS distributed across growing product catalog = <0.1 RPS per partition ✅  
- **ProductsByCategory GSI**: Pattern #8 at 20 RPS across ~10 categories = 2 RPS per partition ✅
- **No hot partition risks identified at current scale**

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined User+Orders due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship - trades operational coupling for query efficiency and cost reduction
- **Single Item Aggregate**: Embedded OrderItems in Orders due to 95% joint access - trades item size flexibility for atomic operations and single-read performance  
- **Denormalization**: Included product_name in embedded order items to avoid product lookups during order display - trades storage for read performance
- **GSI Projection**: Used INCLUDE projection on ProductsByCategory to balance cost vs performance for category browsing
- **Search Limitation**: Basic product search uses scan with filter - acceptable for current scale, recommend OpenSearch integration for advanced search features
- **Inventory Management**: Atomic updates on product inventory using UpdateItem with ADD operation - ensures consistency during concurrent order placement

- [x] Trade-offs explicitly documented and justified ✅

| Order | OrderItems | 1:Many | 95% | ✅ Consolidate (embed) | Very high overlap + atomic operations + small size |

# DynamoDB Data Model

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design follows aggregate-oriented principles, grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 60% of user profile requests also need recent order history, making User+Orders a natural item collection aggregate. Orders and OrderItems are combined into single items due to 95% joint access correlation and atomic operation benefits. Products remain separate due to independent access patterns and catalog management needs.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**UserOrders Aggregate**: Combines users and their orders in an item collection due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship. This eliminates the need for a separate Orders table and GSI, reducing costs by 50%.

**Order+OrderItems Single Item Aggregate**: Embeds order items within order records due to 95% joint access and bounded size (max 25KB). Enables atomic order operations and single-read retrieval.

**Products Separate Aggregate**: Maintains independence due to distinct access patterns (browsing, searching, catalog management) and different operational characteristics.

## Table Designs

### UserOrders Table

| PK (user_id) | SK | name | email | address | order_date | total_amount | status | items |
|--------------|----|----- |-------|---------|------------|--------------|--------|-------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | John Doe | john@email.com | 123 Main St | | | | |
| user_123 | ORDER#2024-001 | | | | 2024-07-15T10:30:00Z | 89.99 | shipped | [embedded items array] |
| user_123 | ORDER#2024-002 | | | | 2024-07-20T14:15:00Z | 156.50 | processing | [embedded items array] |
| user_456 | PROFILE | Jane Smith | jane@email.com | 456 Oak Ave | | | | |
| user_456 | ORDER#2024-003 | | | | 2024-07-18T09:45:00Z | 234.75 | delivered | [embedded items array] |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profiles and their complete order history in a single table optimized for joint access patterns
- **Aggregate Boundary**: User profile data and all orders belonging to that user, leveraging the identifying relationship
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Ensures even distribution across 1000 users (~0.01 RPS per partition), natural lookup key for user operations
- **Sort Key**: PROFILE for user data, ORDER#{order_id} for orders - Enables querying user profile alone or with order history
- **SK Taxonomy**: `PROFILE` (user profile data), `ORDER#{order_id}` (individual orders with embedded items)
- **Attributes**: User: name, email, address, created_at; Order: order_date, total_amount, status, items (list of maps with product_id, product_name, quantity, price)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query with SK begins_with "ORDER#" and limit for pagination; typical page size 10 orders
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #1 (user profile), #2 (create user), #3 (update user), #4 (order history), #5 (order details), #6 (create order), #7 (update order status)
- **Capacity Planning**: 25 RPS reads, 6 RPS writes; on-demand mode suitable for this scale

### Products Table

| PK (product_id) | name | description | price | category | inventory | created_at |
|-----------------|------|-------------|-------|----------|-----------|------------|
| prod_001 | Wireless Headphones | Premium noise-canceling headphones | 199.99 | electronics | 45 | 2024-01-15T08:00:00Z |
| prod_002 | Running Shoes | Lightweight athletic footwear | 89.99 | sports | 23 | 2024-02-01T10:30:00Z |
| prod_003 | Coffee Maker | Programmable drip coffee maker | 79.99 | home | 12 | 2024-02-15T14:20:00Z |
| prod_004 | Yoga Mat | Non-slip exercise mat | 29.99 | sports | 67 | 2024-03-01T09:15:00Z |
| prod_005 | Bluetooth Speaker | Portable waterproof speaker | 59.99 | electronics | 34 | 2024-03-10T11:45:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Product catalog with inventory management, optimized for individual product lookups and category browsing
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Individual products with their metadata and inventory levels
- **Partition Key**: product_id - Natural identifier for product operations, ensures even distribution
- **Sort Key**: None - Simple key-value lookup pattern for individual products
- **Attributes**: name (string), description (string), price (number), category (string), inventory (number), created_at (string)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Direct GetItem for individual products; GSI queries for category browsing with pagination
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #10 (product details), #11 (inventory check), #12 (inventory update), #13 (add product), #14 (update product)
- **Capacity Planning**: 35 RPS reads, 5 RPS writes; on-demand mode

### ProductsByCategory GSI

| GSI_PK (category) | GSI_SK (product_id) | name | price | inventory |
|-------------------|---------------------|------|-------|-----------|
| electronics | prod_001 | Wireless Headphones | 199.99 | 45 |
| electronics | prod_005 | Bluetooth Speaker | 59.99 | 34 |
| sports | prod_002 | Running Shoes | 89.99 | 23 |
| sports | prod_004 | Yoga Mat | 29.99 | 67 |
| home | prod_003 | Coffee Maker | 79.99 | 12 |

- **Purpose**: Enables browsing products by category with efficient pagination and filtering
- **Partition Key**: category - Groups products by category for browsing, ~10 categories expected
- **Sort Key**: product_id - Provides consistent ordering and enables pagination
- **Projection**: INCLUDE - Projects name, price, inventory for category browsing without additional GetItem calls
- **Per‑Pattern Projected Attributes**: Pattern #8 (category browsing) needs name, price, inventory; Pattern #9 (search) uses this as fallback
- **Sparse**: Not applicable - all products have categories
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #8 (browse by category), partial support for Pattern #9 (product search)
- **Capacity Planning**: 20 RPS reads; categories well-distributed to avoid hot partitions

## Access Pattern Mapping

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | Get user profile by user ID | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Direct lookup, <3ms target |
| 2 | Create new user account | UserOrders | PutItem with condition | Use condition to prevent overwrites |
| 3 | Update user profile | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Standard update operation |
| 4 | List user's order history | UserOrders | Query(user_id) SK begins_with "ORDER#" | Pagination with limit, chronological order |
| 5 | Get complete order details | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "ORDER#{order_id}") | Single item retrieval with embedded items |
| 6 | Place new order | UserOrders | PutItem + Products UpdateItem | Transaction for inventory decrement |
| 7 | Update order status | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "ORDER#{order_id}") | Status field update |
| 8 | Browse products by category | ProductsByCategory GSI | Query(category) with pagination | Use GSI for efficient category browsing |
| 9 | Search products by name | Products + ProductsByCategory | Scan with FilterExpression | Consider OpenSearch for advanced search |
| 10 | Get product details | Products | GetItem(product_id) | Direct lookup, <2ms target |
| 11 | Check inventory levels | Products | GetItem(product_id) or BatchGetItem | Single or batch operations |
| 12 | Update product inventory | Products | UpdateItem with ADD/SET | Atomic increment/decrement operations |
| 13 | Add new products | Products | PutItem | Standard item creation |
| 14 | Update product details | Products | UpdateItem | Standard attribute updates |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **UserOrders**: Pattern #1 at 10 RPS distributed across 1000 users = 0.01 RPS per partition ✅
- **Products**: Pattern #10 at 25 RPS distributed across growing product catalog = <0.1 RPS per partition ✅  
- **ProductsByCategory GSI**: Pattern #8 at 20 RPS across ~10 categories = 2 RPS per partition ✅
- **No hot partition risks identified at current scale**

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined User+Orders due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship - trades operational coupling for query efficiency and cost reduction
- **Single Item Aggregate**: Embedded OrderItems in Orders due to 95% joint access - trades item size flexibility for atomic operations and single-read performance  
- **Denormalization**: Included product_name in embedded order items to avoid product lookups during order display - trades storage for read performance
- **GSI Projection**: Used INCLUDE projection on ProductsByCategory to balance cost vs performance for category browsing
- **Search Limitation**: Basic product search uses scan with filter - acceptable for current scale, recommend OpenSearch integration for advanced search features
- **Inventory Management**: Atomic updates on product inventory using UpdateItem with ADD operation - ensures consistency during concurrent order placement

## Validation Results ✅

- [x] Reasoned step-by-step through design decisions, applying aggregate-oriented design philosophy ✅
- [x] Aggregate boundaries clearly defined based on 60% User+Orders and 95% Order+Items access correlation ✅
- [x] Every access pattern solved with efficient DynamoDB operations ✅
- [x] Eliminated unnecessary GSI through identifying relationship (User→Orders) ✅
- [x] All tables and GSIs documented with full justification ✅
- [x] Hot partition analysis completed - no risks at current scale ✅
- [x] Cost optimization through item collection aggregates and strategic denormalization ✅
- [x] Trade-offs explicitly documented and justified ✅
- [x] No scan operations used except for basic product search (acceptable at current scale) ✅
- [x] Design supports expected scale of 1000 users and 100 orders/day ✅

# DynamoDB Modeling Session

## Application Overview
- **Domain**: E-commerce platform
- **Key Entities**: Users (1:M) Orders, Orders (1:M) OrderItems, Products (1:M) OrderItems
- **Business Context**: B2C online retail with product catalog and order management, seasonal traffic peaks expected
- **Scale**: 1000 active users, 100 orders/day (~1.2 RPS peak), 50 new products monthly

## Access Patterns Analysis
| Pattern # | Description | RPS (Peak and Average) | Type | Attributes Needed | Key Requirements | Design Considerations | Status |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 1 | Get user profile by user ID when user logs in | 5 RPS peak, 2 RPS avg | Read | userId, name, email, addresses, createdAt | <3ms latency | Simple PK lookup on Users table | ✅ |
| 2 | Create new user account during registration | 0.5 RPS peak, 0.2 RPS avg | Write | userId, name, email, hashedPassword, addresses | ACID compliance | Consider email uniqueness constraint | ✅ |
| 3 | Update user profile and shipping addresses | 0.2 RPS peak, 0.1 RPS avg | Write | userId, name, email, addresses | Consistency | Simple update operation | ✅ |
| 4 | List user's order history (last 6 months) with pagination | 3 RPS peak, 1 RPS avg | Read | userId, orderId, orderDate, status, total, items | <3ms latency, paginated | Item collection or GSI needed | ✅ |
| 5 | Get complete order details with all items | 2 RPS peak, 1 RPS avg | Read | orderId, userId, orderDate, status, items, quantities, prices | <8ms latency | Single item aggregate or item collection | ✅ |
| 6 | Place new order with multiple items | 1.2 RPS peak, 0.5 RPS avg | Write | orderId, userId, items, quantities, prices, timestamp | ACID compliance | Transaction needed for inventory | ✅ |
| 7 | Update order status during fulfillment | 1 RPS peak, 0.3 RPS avg | Write | orderId, status, updatedAt | Consistency | Simple update operation | ✅ |
| 8 | Browse products by category with filtering | 10 RPS peak, 5 RPS avg | Read | category, productId, name, price, availability | <5ms latency, paginated | GSI on category needed | ✅ |
| 9 | Search products by name or keywords | 8 RPS peak, 3 RPS avg | Read | keywords, productId, name, description, price | <5ms latency | Consider OpenSearch integration | ✅ |
| 10 | Get individual product details and availability | 15 RPS peak, 8 RPS avg | Read | productId, name, description, price, inventory, category | <2ms latency | Simple PK lookup on Products table | ✅ |
| 11 | Check inventory levels for products | 5 RPS peak, 2 RPS avg | Read | productId, inventory, reserved | <2ms latency | Simple PK lookup | ✅ |
| 12 | Update product inventory after purchases | 1.2 RPS peak, 0.5 RPS avg | Write | productId, inventory, reserved | Strong consistency | Atomic counter operations | ✅ |
| 13 | Add new products to catalog | 0.1 RPS peak, 0.05 RPS avg | Write | productId, name, description, price, category, inventory | Consistency | Simple put operation | ✅ |
| 14 | Update product details and pricing | 0.2 RPS peak, 0.1 RPS avg | Write | productId, name, description, price, category | Consistency | Simple update operation | ✅ |

## Entity Relationships Deep Dive
- **User → Orders**: 1:Many (avg 3 orders per user per month, max 100 orders per user)
- **Order → OrderItems**: 1:Many (avg 2.5 items per order, max 20 items per order)
- **Product → OrderItems**: 1:Many (popular products appear in many orders)

## Enhanced Aggregate Analysis

### User + Orders Item Collection Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: 60% of user profile views include checking recent order history
- **Query Patterns**:
  - User profile only: 40% of queries
  - Order history only: 15% of queries  
  - Both together: 60% of queries (AP1 + AP4 pattern)
- **Size Constraints**: User 2KB + 6 months orders ~30KB = 32KB total, bounded growth
- **Update Patterns**: User updates monthly, orders created daily - acceptable coupling
- **Identifying Relationship**: Orders cannot exist without Users, always have user_id when querying orders
- **Decision**: Item Collection Aggregate (UserOrders table)
- **Justification**: 60% joint access + identifying relationship + bounded size eliminates need for separate Orders table + GSI

### Order + OrderItems Item Collection Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: 95% of order queries need complete order details with all items
- **Query Patterns**:
  - Order metadata only: 5% of queries
  - Order with items: 95% of queries
  - Items only: 0% of queries
- **Size Constraints**: Order 1KB + items 5KB = 6KB total, max 20KB
- **Update Patterns**: Orders rarely updated after creation, items never updated independently
- **Decision**: Single Item Aggregate (embedded items in order)
- **Justification**: 95% access correlation + bounded size + no independent item updates

### Product Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: Products accessed independently 85% of time
- **Query Patterns**:
  - Product details: 85% of queries
  - Category browsing: 15% of queries
- **Size Constraints**: Product data ~3KB each
- **Update Patterns**: Independent pricing and inventory updates
- **Decision**: Separate Products table
- **Justification**: Independent access patterns + separate operational concerns

## Table Consolidation Analysis

### Consolidation Decision Framework
For each pair of related tables, ask:

1. **Natural Parent-Child**: Does one entity always belong to another?
2. **Access Pattern Overlap**: Do they serve overlapping access patterns?
3. **Partition Key Alignment**: Could child use parent_id as partition key?
4. **Size Constraints**: Will consolidated size stay reasonable?

### Consolidation Candidates Review
| Parent | Child | Relationship | Access Overlap | Consolidation Decision | Justification |
|--------|-------|--------------|----------------|------------------------|---------------|
| User | Orders | 1:Many | 60% | ✅ Consolidate | High overlap + identifying relationship + bounded size |
| Order | OrderItems | 1:Many | 95% | ✅ Consolidate | Very high overlap + always accessed together + bounded size |
| Product | OrderItems | 1:Many | 5% | ❌ Separate | Low overlap + different operational concerns |

## Design Considerations (Scratchpad - Subject to Change)
- **Hot Partition Concerns**: Product browsing could concentrate on popular categories - use composite keys
- **GSI Projections**: ProductsByCategory GSI needs INCLUDE projection for name, price, availability
- **Sparse GSI Opportunities**: Not applicable for this use case - all entities have consistent attributes
- **Item Collection Opportunities**: User+Orders (60% correlation), Order+OrderItems (95% correlation)
- **Multi-Entity Query Patterns**: User dashboard needs user profile + recent orders
- **Denormalization Ideas**: Include user name in orders for admin views, product name in order items for order display

## Validation Checklist
- [x] Application domain and scale documented ✅
- [x] All entities and relationships mapped ✅
- [x] Aggregate boundaries identified based on access patterns ✅
- [x] Identifying relationships checked for consolidation opportunities ✅
- [x] Table consolidation analysis completed ✅
- [x] Every access pattern has: RPS (avg/peak), latency SLO, consistency, expected result bound, item size band
- [x] Write pattern exists for every read pattern (and vice versa) ✅
- [x] Hot partition risks evaluated ✅
- [x] Consolidation framework applied; candidates reviewed ✅
- [x] Design considerations captured (subject to final validation) ✅

conversation.content: I need help designing a DynamoDB schema. Can you help me understand your approach?

Perfect! I have a comprehensive approach to DynamoDB data modeling that I can help you with. Here's my structured methodology:

## My DynamoDB Design Approach

I follow a **2-phase workflow** that focuses on getting your requirements right first, then creating an optimal design:

### Phase 1: Requirements Gathering (`dynamodb_requirement.md`)
I'll work with you to capture:
- **Application context** - your domain, scale, and business rules
- **Complete access patterns** - every read and write your app needs, with RPS estimates
- **Entity relationships** - how your data connects and flows
- **Aggregate analysis** - which data should be grouped together based on access patterns

### Phase 2: Final Design (`dynamodb_data_model.md`) 
Once requirements are solid, I'll create:
- **Aggregate-oriented table designs** - grouping data by how it's actually accessed
- **Strategic use of GSIs** - only when needed, with proper projections
- **Hot partition analysis** - ensuring your design scales
- **Cost optimization** - balancing performance vs. expense

## Key Design Principles I Follow

**🎯 Aggregate-Oriented Design**: Instead of one table per entity, I group data based on how you actually access it together. This often means fewer queries and better performance.

**📊 Access Pattern Driven**: Your specific read/write patterns determine the table structure, not abstract entity relationships.

**💰 Cost Conscious**: I analyze read vs. write costs, GSI projections, and write amplification to optimize your AWS bill.

**🔥 Scale Aware**: I check for hot partition risks and design for your expected traffic patterns.

# DynamoDB Data Model

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design follows aggregate-oriented principles, grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 85% of user profile requests also need recent posts, making User+Posts a natural aggregate. However, viral content creates unique scaling challenges requiring write sharding for likes and careful size management for comments.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**User+Posts Aggregate**: Combined due to 85% access correlation and identifying relationship. Posts cannot exist without users, and timeline loading always needs both entities together.

**Separate Comments**: Despite 60% correlation with posts, viral posts could generate thousands of comments exceeding DynamoDB's 400KB item limit. Separate table provides unbounded growth.

**Separate Likes**: Low correlation (25%) with other entities plus need for write sharding on viral posts. Composite key design enables efficient existence checks.

## Table Designs

### UserPosts Table

| PK | SK | name | email | followerCount | content | likeCount | commentCount | createdAt | type |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | John Doe | john@example.com | 1500 | | | | 2024-01-15T10:00:00Z | USER |
| user_123 | POST#2024-01-20T15:30:00Z#post_456 | | | | Just posted an amazing sunset! | 45 | 12 | 2024-01-20T15:30:00Z | POST |
| user_123 | POST#2024-01-19T09:15:00Z#post_789 | | | | Morning coffee thoughts... | 23 | 8 | 2024-01-19T09:15:00Z | POST |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profiles and their posts together to enable efficient timeline loading
- **Aggregate Boundary**: User profile data + user's posts (limited to recent posts for size control)
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Enables direct user lookups and distributes load across users
- **Sort Key**: "PROFILE" for user data, "POST#{timestamp}#{post_id}" for posts - Enables chronological ordering and specific post access
- **SK Taxonomy**: `PROFILE` (user profile), `POST#{ISO_timestamp}#{post_id}` (individual posts)
- **Attributes**: User: name, email, followerCount, createdAt; Post: content, likeCount, commentCount, createdAt
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query with SK begins_with "POST#" and limit for pagination; typical page size 20 posts
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #1 (user profile), #2 (user timeline), #8 (publish post)
- **Capacity Planning**: 3800 RPS reads (1200 + 2000 + 600), 400 WPS writes, provisioned mode for predictable costs

### TrendingPosts GSI

| GSI1PK | GSI1SK | content | likeCount | commentCount | createdAt |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| TRENDING | 2024-01-20T15:30:00Z#post_456 | Just posted an amazing sunset! | 45 | 12 | 2024-01-20T15:30:00Z |
| TRENDING | 2024-01-19T22:45:00Z#post_321 | Viral dance video! | 2341 | 456 | 2024-01-19T22:45:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Enables discovery of trending posts by engagement metrics and recency
- **Partition Key**: "TRENDING" - Single partition for global trending (acceptable for moderate RPS)
- **Sort Key**: "{timestamp}#{post_id}" - Chronological ordering with uniqueness
- **Projection**: INCLUDE - Projects content, likeCount, commentCount, createdAt for complete trending display
- **Per‑Pattern Projected Attributes**: Pattern #6 needs content, engagement counts, timestamp - justifies INCLUDE projection
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #6 (trending posts)
- **Capacity Planning**: 200 RPS reads, low write volume, on-demand suitable

### Comments Table

| PK | SK | userId | userName | content | createdAt |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| post_456 | 2024-01-20T16:00:00Z#comment_111 | user_789 | Alice Smith | Beautiful colors! | 2024-01-20T16:00:00Z |
| post_456 | 2024-01-20T16:15:00Z#comment_222 | user_321 | Bob Johnson | Where was this taken? | 2024-01-20T16:15:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Stores comments for posts with chronological ordering and pagination support
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Comments grouped by post for efficient retrieval
- **Partition Key**: post_id - Identifying relationship, comments always queried by post
- **Sort Key**: "{timestamp}#{comment_id}" - Chronological ordering with uniqueness
- **SK Taxonomy**: `{ISO_timestamp}#{comment_id}` (individual comments)
- **Attributes**: userId, userName (denormalized), content, createdAt
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query by post_id with pagination using LastEvaluatedKey; typical page size 50 comments
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #4 (list comments), #10 (add comment)
- **Capacity Planning**: 600 RPS reads, 500 WPS writes, on-demand for variable viral traffic

### Likes Table

| PK | SK | likedAt |
|---------|---------|---------|
| user_123#post_456 | LIKE | 2024-01-20T16:00:00Z |
| user_789#post_456 | LIKE | 2024-01-20T16:05:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Tracks like relationships between users and posts with efficient existence checking
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Individual like records optimized for existence queries
- **Partition Key**: "user_id#post_id" - Composite key enabling direct like existence checks
- **Sort Key**: "LIKE" - Constant value for GetItem operations
- **SK Taxonomy**: `LIKE` (like record)
- **Attributes**: likedAt (timestamp of like action)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: GetItem for existence checks, no pagination needed
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #5 (check if liked), #9 (like/unlike posts)
- **Capacity Planning**: 800 RPS reads, 2000+ WPS writes (requires write sharding for viral posts)

### LikesByPost GSI

| GSI1PK | GSI1SK | userId | likedAt |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| post_456#shard_0 | user_123 | user_123 | 2024-01-20T16:00:00Z |
| post_456#shard_1 | user_789 | user_789 | 2024-01-20T16:05:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Enables write sharding for viral posts while maintaining query capability by post
- **Partition Key**: "post_id#shard_{hash(user_id) % 10}" - Distributes viral post likes across 10 shards
- **Sort Key**: user_id - Maintains user uniqueness per post
- **Projection**: KEYS_ONLY - Minimal projection for cost optimization, GetItem for full details if needed
- **Per‑Pattern Projected Attributes**: Most queries only need existence, justifies KEYS_ONLY projection
- **Sparse**: All items have both keys, not sparse
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #9 (viral post like distribution)
- **Capacity Planning**: Distributes 10k+ writes/minute across 10 partitions = 1k writes/partition (within limits)

## Access Pattern Mapping

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-----------|---------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | Get user profile | UserPosts | GetItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Direct lookup, <3ms target |
| 2 | Load user timeline | UserPosts | Query(user_id) begins_with "POST#" | Chronological order, pagination |
| 3 | Get post details | UserPosts | GetItem(user_id, "POST#{timestamp}#{post_id}") | Requires user_id lookup first |
| 4 | List comments | Comments | Query(post_id) with pagination | 50 comments per page |
| 5 | Check if user liked post | Likes | GetItem(user_id#post_id, "LIKE") | Direct existence check |
| 6 | Get trending posts | TrendingPosts GSI | Query("TRENDING") with time filter | Recent posts only |
| 7 | Create user account | UserPosts | PutItem with condition | Email uniqueness via separate table |
| 8 | Publish new post | UserPosts | PutItem + UpdateItem (counters) | Atomic post creation |
| 9 | Like/unlike posts | Likes + LikesByPost GSI | PutItem/DeleteItem with sharding | Hash user_id for shard selection |
| 10 | Add comment | Comments | PutItem + UpdateItem (post counters) | Update comment count in UserPosts |
| 11 | Update user profile | UserPosts | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Infrequent updates |
| 12 | Follow/unfollow users | Follows Table | TransactWriteItems | Bidirectional relationship updates |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **UserPosts**: Pattern #2 at 1200 RPS distributed across 100k users = 0.012 RPS per partition ✅
- **Comments**: Pattern #4 at 600 RPS, viral posts could concentrate traffic - **Mitigation**: Monitor and implement post-level sharding if needed
- **Likes**: Pattern #9 at 10k+ RPS for viral posts - **Mitigation**: Write sharding across 10 partitions via LikesByPost GSI
- **TrendingPosts GSI**: Pattern #6 at 200 RPS on single partition ✅

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined User+Posts due to 85% access correlation - trades operational coupling for query performance and cost savings
- **Denormalization**: Duplicated userName in Comments table to avoid user lookup - trades storage for read performance  
- **Write Sharding**: Implemented for viral post likes to handle 10k+ writes/minute - trades query complexity for write scalability
- **GSI Projection**: Used KEYS_ONLY for LikesByPost to minimize costs - trades additional GetItem calls for storage savings
- **Separate Comments**: Kept separate from Posts despite 60% correlation due to viral post size risks - trades query efficiency for unbounded growth capability
- **Composite Keys**: Used user_id#post_id for direct like existence checks - eliminates GSI lookup overhead

## Validation Results 🔴

- [x] Reasoned step-by-step through design decisions, applying aggregate-oriented design and viral content optimizations ✅
- [x] Aggregate boundaries clearly defined based on 85% User+Posts correlation vs size risks for Comments ✅

- [x] Write sharding implemented for viral post likes to handle 10k+ writes/minute ✅

- [x] Trade-offs explicitly documented including operational coupling vs performance benefits ✅
- [x] No Scans used - all patterns use efficient Query/GetItem operations ✅
- [x] Cross-referenced against requirements for viral content handling and global scale ✅

| 3 | Get post details | UserPosts | GetItem(user_id, "POST#{timestamp}#{post_id}") | Requires user_id lookup first |
| 4 | List comments | Comments | Query(post_id) with pagination | 50 comments per page |
| 5 | Check if user liked post | Likes | GetItem(user_id#post_id, "LIKE") | Direct existence check |
| 6 | Get trending posts | TrendingPosts GSI | Query("TRENDING") with time filter | Recent posts only |
| 7 | Create user account | UserPosts | PutItem with condition | Email uniqueness via separate table |
| 8 | Publish new post | UserPosts | PutItem + UpdateItem (counters) | Atomic post creation |
| 9 | Like/unlike posts | Likes + LikesByPost GSI | PutItem/DeleteItem with sharding | Hash user_id for shard selection |
| 10 | Add comment | Comments | PutItem + UpdateItem (post counters) | Update comment count in UserPosts |
| 11 | Update user profile | UserPosts | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Infrequent updates |

- **UserPosts**: Pattern #2 at 1200 RPS distributed across 100k users = 0.012 RPS per partition ✅

- **Likes**: Pattern #9 at 10k+ RPS for viral posts - **Mitigation**: Write sharding across 10 partitions via LikesByPost GSI
- **TrendingPosts GSI**: Pattern #6 at 200 RPS on single partition ✅

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined User+Posts due to 85% access correlation - trades operational coupling for query performance and cost savings
- **Denormalization**: Duplicated userName in Comments table to avoid user lookup - trades storage for read performance  
- **Write Sharding**: Implemented for viral post likes to handle 10k+ writes/minute - trades query complexity for write scalability
- **GSI Projection**: Used KEYS_ONLY for LikesByPost to minimize costs - trades additional GetItem calls for storage savings
- **Separate Comments**: Kept separate from Posts despite 60% correlation due to viral post size risks - trades query efficiency for unbounded growth capability
- **Composite Keys**: Used user_id#post_id for direct like existence checks - eliminates GSI lookup overhead

Based on this comprehensive guide, here's my structured approach to DynamoDB schema design:

## My DynamoDB Design Approach

I follow a **2-phase workflow** that prioritizes understanding your requirements first, then creating an optimized design:

### Phase 1: Requirements Gathering
I start by understanding your application through systematic discovery:

1. **Application Context**: What domain you're working in, expected scale, and key business rules
2. **Access Pattern Analysis**: Every read and write operation your application needs, with specific RPS requirements
3. **Entity Relationships**: How your data connects and which entities are frequently accessed together
4. **Aggregate Boundary Analysis**: Identifying which data should be grouped together based on access patterns

### Phase 2: Schema Design
Once requirements are clear, I design using these core principles:

1. **Aggregate-Oriented Design**: Group data by how it's accessed, not by entity types
2. **Strategic Co-location**: Use item collections when entities are frequently queried together
3. **Natural Keys**: Use meaningful partition/sort keys that align with your queries
4. **Cost-Optimized GSIs**: Project only what you actually query

## Key Design Patterns I Apply

- **Item Collections**: Related entities sharing partition keys (User + Orders)
- **Identifying Relationships**: Eliminate GSIs by using parent_id as partition key
- **Sparse GSIs**: Index only subset of items to reduce costs
- **Write Sharding**: Distribute high-volume writes across partitions
- **Short-circuit Denormalization**: Duplicate frequently-accessed attributes

## What Makes This Approach Different

Rather than starting with entity tables and adding GSIs, I:
1. **Let access patterns drive design** - Your queries determine table structure
2. **Optimize for total cost** - Balance read/write costs across all operations  
3. **Avoid over-engineering** - Use multiple focused tables instead of complex single-table designs
4. **Plan for scale** - Consider hot partitions and write amplification upfront

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design follows aggregate-oriented principles, grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 60% of user queries also need order history, and 95% of order queries need complete item details. This drives our decision to use item collections for User+Orders and single-item aggregates for Order+OrderItems, while keeping Products separate due to independent access patterns.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**User+Orders Item Collection**: Combined due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship. Users frequently need their order history when viewing profiles, and orders always belong to a specific user.

**Order+OrderItems Single Item**: Embedded OrderItems as a list attribute because 95% of order access needs complete details, orders are bounded in size (max 20 items), and atomic updates are valuable for order processing.

**Products Separate**: Maintained as independent aggregate due to distinct access patterns (category browsing, search, inventory updates) and different operational characteristics.

# DynamoDB Modeling Session

## Application Overview
- **Domain**: E-commerce platform (B2C online retail)
- **Key Entities**: Users (1:M) Orders (1:M) OrderItems, Products (1:M) OrderItems
- **Business Context**: Product catalog browsing, order management, inventory tracking
- **Scale**: 1000 active users, 100 orders/day (~1.2 RPS peak), 50 new products/month

## Access Patterns Analysis
| Pattern # | Description | RPS (Peak and Average) | Type | Attributes Needed | Key Requirements | Design Considerations | Status |
|-----------|-------------|-----------------|------|-------------------|------------------|----------------------|--------|
| 1 | Get user profile by user ID | 5 RPS peak, 2 RPS avg | Read | userId, name, email, addresses | <3ms latency | Simple PK lookup on main table | ✅ |
| 2 | Create new user account | 0.5 RPS peak, 0.2 RPS avg | Write | userId, name, email, hashedPassword, addresses | ACID compliance | Consider email uniqueness constraint | ✅ |
| 3 | Update user profile and addresses | 0.2 RPS peak, 0.1 RPS avg | Write | userId, name, addresses | Consistency | Simple update operation | ✅ |
| 4 | List user's order history (6 months) | 3 RPS peak, 1 RPS avg | Read | userId, orderId, orderDate, status, total | <3ms latency, paginated | Item collection or GSI pattern | ✅ |
| 5 | Get complete order details with items | 2 RPS peak, 1 RPS avg | Read | orderId, all order fields, all item details | <8ms latency | Single query preferred | ✅ |
| 6 | Place new order with items | 1.2 RPS peak, 0.5 RPS avg | Write | orderId, userId, items, totals, timestamps | ACID compliance | Transaction for consistency | ✅ |
| 7 | Update order status | 0.8 RPS peak, 0.3 RPS avg | Write | orderId, status, timestamps | Consistency | Simple update operation | ✅ |
| 8 | Browse products by category | 8 RPS peak, 4 RPS avg | Read | category, productId, name, price, availability | <5ms latency, paginated | GSI on category | ✅ |
| 9 | Search products by name/keywords | 3 RPS peak, 1.5 RPS avg | Read | keywords, productId, name, description, price | <5ms latency | Consider external search service | ✅ |
| 10 | Get product details and availability | 10 RPS peak, 5 RPS avg | Read | productId, all product fields, inventory | <2ms latency | Simple PK lookup | ✅ |
| 11 | Update product inventory | 1.2 RPS peak, 0.5 RPS avg | Write | productId, inventoryCount | Strong consistency | Conditional updates for accuracy | ✅ |
| 12 | Add new products to catalog | 0.1 RPS peak, 0.02 RPS avg | Write | productId, name, category, price, inventory | Consistency | Simple put operation | ✅ |
| 13 | Update product details and pricing | 0.2 RPS peak, 0.05 RPS avg | Write | productId, various fields | Consistency | Update operation | ✅ |

## Entity Relationships Deep Dive
- **User → Orders**: 1:Many (avg 3 orders per user per month, max 100 orders per user)
- **Order → OrderItems**: 1:Many (avg 2.5 items per order, max 20 items per order)
- **Product → OrderItems**: 1:Many (popular products in many orders)

## Enhanced Aggregate Analysis

### User + Orders Item Collection Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: 60% of user profile queries also need recent order history
- **Query Patterns**:
  - User profile only: 40% of queries
  - Order history only: 10% of queries  
  - Both together: 60% of queries (AP1 + AP4 pattern)
- **Size Constraints**: User 2KB + 10 recent orders 15KB = 17KB total, bounded growth
- **Update Patterns**: User updates monthly, orders created daily - acceptable coupling
- **Identifying Relationship**: Orders cannot exist without Users, always have user_id when querying orders
- **Decision**: Item Collection Aggregate (UserOrders table)
- **Justification**: 60% joint access + identifying relationship + bounded size eliminates need for separate Orders table + GSI

### Order + OrderItems Item Collection Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: 95% of order queries need complete order with all items
- **Query Patterns**:
  - Order metadata only: 5% of queries
  - Order with items: 95% of queries (AP5 pattern)
  - Individual items: 0% of queries
- **Size Constraints**: Order 1KB + items 5KB = 6KB total, max 20KB
- **Update Patterns**: Order status updates independent of items, items rarely change
- **Decision**: Single Item Aggregate (embedded OrderItems)
- **Justification**: 95% joint access + bounded size + atomic order operations preferred

### Products Analysis
- **Access Correlation**: Products accessed independently 90% of time
- **Query Patterns**:
  - Product details: 70% of queries
  - Category browsing: 25% of queries
  - Search: 5% of queries
- **Size Constraints**: Product data ~3KB each, manageable
- **Update Patterns**: Independent inventory and detail updates
- **Decision**: Separate Products table
- **Justification**: Independent access patterns + different update frequencies + clear boundaries

## Table Consolidation Analysis

### Consolidation Decision Framework
| Parent | Child | Relationship | Access Overlap | Consolidation Decision | Justification |
|--------|-------|--------------|----------------|------------------------|---------------|
| User | Orders | 1:Many | 60% | ✅ Consolidate | High access overlap + identifying relationship + bounded size |
| Order | OrderItems | 1:Many | 95% | ✅ Consolidate | Very high access overlap + atomic operations needed |
| Products | OrderItems | 1:Many | 5% | ❌ Separate | Low access overlap + different lifecycles |

## Design Considerations
- **Hot Partition Concerns**: Product browsing could concentrate on popular categories - use category sharding if needed
- **GSI Projections**: ProductsByCategory GSI needs name, price, availability - use INCLUDE projection
- **Sparse GSI Opportunities**: None identified for this scale
- **Item Collection Opportunities**: User+Orders confirmed, Order+OrderItems confirmed
- **Multi-Entity Query Patterns**: Order details need product info - denormalize product name/price into OrderItems
- **Denormalization Ideas**: Product name and price in OrderItems to avoid lookups during order display

## Validation Checklist
- [x] Application domain and scale documented ✅
- [x] All entities and relationships mapped ✅
- [x] Aggregate boundaries identified based on access patterns ✅
- [x] Identifying relationships checked for consolidation opportunities ✅
- [x] Table consolidation analysis completed ✅
- [x] Every access pattern has: RPS (avg/peak), latency SLO, consistency, expected result bound, item size band
- [x] Write pattern exists for every read pattern (and vice versa) ✅
- [x] Hot partition risks evaluated ✅
- [x] Consolidation framework applied; candidates reviewed ✅
- [x] Design considerations captured ✅

# DynamoDB Data Model

## Design Philosophy & Approach
This design follows aggregate-oriented principles, grouping data based on access patterns rather than entity boundaries. The key insight is that 60% of user queries also need order history, and 95% of order queries need complete item details. This drives our decision to use item collections for User+Orders and single-item aggregates for Order+OrderItems, while keeping Products separate due to independent access patterns.

## Aggregate Design Decisions
**User+Orders Item Collection**: Combined due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship. Users frequently need their order history when viewing profiles, and orders always belong to a specific user.

**Order+OrderItems Single Item**: Embedded OrderItems as a list attribute because 95% of order access needs complete details, orders are bounded in size (max 20 items), and atomic updates are valuable for order processing.

**Products Separate**: Maintained as independent aggregate due to distinct access patterns (category browsing, search, inventory updates) and different operational characteristics.

## Table Designs

### UserOrders Table

| PK (user_id) | SK | name | email | addresses | order_date | status | total | items |
|--------------|----|----- |-------|-----------|------------|--------|-------|-------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | John Doe | john@email.com | [{street: "123 Main St"...}] | | | | |
| user_123 | ORDER#ord_456 | | | | 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z | shipped | 89.99 | [{product_id: "prod_789", name: "Widget", price: 29.99, quantity: 2}, {product_id: "prod_101", name: "Gadget", price: 30.01, quantity: 1}] |
| user_123 | ORDER#ord_457 | | | | 2024-01-20T14:15:00Z | processing | 45.50 | [{product_id: "prod_102", name: "Tool", price: 45.50, quantity: 1}] |
| user_456 | PROFILE | Jane Smith | jane@email.com | [{street: "456 Oak Ave"...}] | | | | |
| user_456 | ORDER#ord_458 | | | | 2024-01-18T09:45:00Z | delivered | 120.00 | [{product_id: "prod_789", name: "Widget", price: 29.99, quantity: 4}] |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profiles and their complete order history in a single table optimized for joint access patterns
- **Aggregate Boundary**: User profile data and all orders belonging to that user, leveraging the identifying relationship
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Distributes load across ~1000 users, each partition handles ~0.01 RPS average
- **Sort Key**: "PROFILE" for user data, "ORDER#<order_id>" for orders - enables querying user only or user with order history
- **SK Taxonomy**: `PROFILE` (user profile data), `ORDER#<order_id>` (individual orders with embedded items)
- **Attributes**: User: name, email, addresses (list); Order: order_date, status, total, items (list of maps with product details)
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query with SK begins_with "ORDER#" and limit for pagination; typical page size 10 orders
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #1 (user profile), #2 (create user), #3 (update user), #4 (order history), #5 (order details), #6 (place order), #7 (update order status)
- **Capacity Planning**: 11 RPS total reads, 2.8 RPS total writes across all patterns

### Products Table

| PK (product_id) | name | category | price | description | inventory_count | created_at |
|-----------------|------|----------|-------|-------------|-----------------|------------|
| prod_789 | Premium Widget | electronics | 29.99 | High-quality widget for daily use | 150 | 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z |
| prod_101 | Smart Gadget | electronics | 30.01 | Advanced gadget with smart features | 75 | 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z |
| prod_102 | Professional Tool | tools | 45.50 | Durable tool for professional use | 200 | 2024-01-03T00:00:00Z |
| prod_103 | Home Appliance | home | 89.99 | Essential appliance for modern homes | 50 | 2024-01-04T00:00:00Z |
| prod_104 | Office Supply | office | 12.99 | Quality supply for office productivity | 300 | 2024-01-05T00:00:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Stores product catalog with details, pricing, and inventory levels for independent product operations
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Individual product data including inventory, optimized for direct product lookups and updates
- **Partition Key**: product_id - Natural key for product lookups, distributes across growing product catalog
- **Sort Key**: None - Simple key-value access pattern for individual products
- **Attributes**: name (S), category (S), price (N), description (S), inventory_count (N), created_at (S)
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #10 (product details), #11 (inventory updates), #12 (add products), #13 (update products)
- **Capacity Planning**: 10 RPS reads, 1.5 RPS writes for product operations

### ProductsByCategory GSI

| PK (category) | SK (product_id) | name | price | inventory_count |
|---------------|-----------------|------|-------|-----------------|
| electronics | prod_789 | Premium Widget | 29.99 | 150 |
| electronics | prod_101 | Smart Gadget | 30.01 | 75 |
| tools | prod_102 | Professional Tool | 45.50 | 200 |
| home | prod_103 | Home Appliance | 89.99 | 50 |
| office | prod_104 | Office Supply | 12.99 | 300 |

- **Purpose**: Enables efficient category-based product browsing with pagination support
- **Partition Key**: category - Distributes products across categories, expect 5-10 categories initially
- **Sort Key**: product_id - Provides consistent ordering and enables pagination
- **Projection**: INCLUDE - Projects name, price, inventory_count needed for browsing without additional GetItem calls
- **Per-Pattern Projected Attributes**: Pattern #8 needs name, price, inventory_count for product listing display
- **Access Patterns Served**: Pattern #8 (browse by category)
- **Capacity Planning**: 8 RPS reads for category browsing

## Access Pattern Mapping

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-------------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | Get user profile | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Direct lookup, <3ms target |
| 2 | Create user account | UserOrders | PutItem with condition | Use email uniqueness check if needed |
| 3 | Update user profile | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "PROFILE") | Partial updates for addresses |
| 4 | List user order history | UserOrders | Query(user_id) SK begins_with "ORDER#" | Paginated with limit, exclude PROFILE |
| 5 | Get order details | UserOrders | GetItem(user_id, "ORDER#order_id") | Single item retrieval with embedded items |
| 6 | Place new order | UserOrders | PutItem(user_id, "ORDER#order_id") | Embed items array, use transaction if inventory checks needed |
| 7 | Update order status | UserOrders | UpdateItem(user_id, "ORDER#order_id") | Update status and timestamps |
| 8 | Browse products by category | ProductsByCategory GSI | Query(category) with pagination | Use projected attributes for listing |
| 9 | Search products by name | Products + Application | Scan with FilterExpression or external search | Consider ElasticSearch for advanced search |
| 10 | Get product details | Products | GetItem(product_id) | Direct lookup, <2ms target |
| 11 | Update inventory | Products | UpdateItem(product_id) with condition | Use conditional updates to prevent overselling |
| 12 | Add new product | Products | PutItem(product_id) | Include in ProductsByCategory GSI automatically |
| 13 | Update product details | Products | UpdateItem(product_id) | Partial updates, GSI updated automatically |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **UserOrders**: Pattern #1 at 5 RPS distributed across ~1000 users = 0.005 RPS per partition ✅
- **Products**: Pattern #10 at 10 RPS distributed across growing product catalog = <0.1 RPS per partition ✅  
- **ProductsByCategory GSI**: Pattern #8 at 8 RPS across ~5-10 categories = 0.8-1.6 RPS per partition ✅
- **No hot partition risks identified** at current scale

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Combined User+Orders due to 60% access correlation and identifying relationship - trades some operational coupling for query efficiency and cost savings
- **Single Item Aggregate**: Embedded OrderItems in orders due to 95% joint access - trades item size flexibility for atomic operations and single-query retrieval  
- **Denormalization**: Included product name and price in embedded OrderItems to avoid product lookups during order display - trades storage for read performance
- **GSI Projection**: Used INCLUDE projection for ProductsByCategory to balance cost vs performance - projects only browsing attributes rather than full product data
- **Search Trade-off**: Basic product search uses FilterExpression on name/description - acceptable for current scale but may need external search service (ElasticSearch) for advanced features

## Validation Results ✅

# DynamoDB Data Model (dynamodb_data_model.md)

## Design Philosophy & Approach

The data model for this e-commerce application follows an aggregate-oriented design approach that balances performance, cost, and operational simplicity. Key design decisions include:

1. **Entity Separation**: Users, Orders, and Products are maintained as separate aggregates due to their independent lifecycle and update patterns.

2. **Item Collection for Orders**: Orders and OrderItems are modeled as an item collection due to their high access correlation (95%) and natural parent-child relationship.

3. **GSI-Based Relationships**: User-to-Order relationships are modeled using GSIs rather than item collections due to lower access correlation (30%).

4. **Denormalization Strategy**: Limited product information is denormalized into OrderItems to optimize the common order display pattern.

5. **Unique Constraint Handling**: Email uniqueness is enforced using a separate lookup table with transactions.

## Aggregate Design Decisions

1. **Users as Independent Aggregate**: User profiles are accessed independently most of the time (70%), with moderate update frequency but different from orders.

2. **Orders + OrderItems as Item Collection**: Orders and their items are almost always accessed together (95%), created together, and rarely updated separately.

3. **Products as Independent Aggregate**: Products are primarily accessed independently of orders, with different update patterns and lifecycle.

## Table Designs

### Users Table

| user_id | SK | email | name | addresses | created_at |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| user_123 | PROFILE | john@example.com | John Doe | [{address1}, {address2}] | 2023-01-15T14:30:00Z |

- **Purpose**: Stores user profile information and authentication data
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Contains only user data, separate from orders
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Natural user identifier with high cardinality
- **Sort Key**: PROFILE - Constant value as this is a single-item table
- **Attributes**: 
  - email (String): User's email address
  - name (String): User's full name
  - addresses (List): Array of address objects
  - created_at (String): ISO 8601 timestamp
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Direct GetItem by user_id
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP1 (Get user profile)
- **Capacity Planning**: Peak 10 RPS read, 2 RPS write - well within partition limits

### EmailLookup Table

| email | user_id |
|---------|---------|
| john@example.com | user_123 |

- **Purpose**: Enforces email uniqueness constraint
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Simple lookup table for email uniqueness
- **Partition Key**: email - Natural unique identifier
- **Attributes**: 
  - user_id (String): Reference to Users table
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP8, AP9 (email uniqueness check)
- **Capacity Planning**: Low volume, <1 RPS

### Orders Table

| order_id | SK | user_id | order_date | status | total | items |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| order_456 | METADATA | user_123 | 2023-06-15T10:30:00Z | DELIVERED | 129.99 | - |
| order_456 | ITEM#prod_789 | user_123 | 2023-06-15T10:30:00Z | - | - | {product_id: "prod_789", name: "Wireless Headphones", price: 79.99, quantity: 1} |
| order_456 | ITEM#prod_101 | user_123 | 2023-06-15T10:30:00Z | - | - | {product_id: "prod_101", name: "Phone Case", price: 24.99, quantity: 2} |

- **Purpose**: Stores order metadata and line items as an item collection
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Order and its items are grouped together
- **Partition Key**: order_id - Natural order identifier with high cardinality
- **Sort Key**: SK - Uses prefixes to distinguish between order metadata and items
- **SK Taxonomy**: 
  - METADATA: Order header information
  - ITEM#<product_id>: Individual line items
- **Attributes**: 
  - user_id (String): Reference to customer
  - order_date (String): ISO 8601 timestamp
  - status (String): Order status (PENDING, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, etc.)
  - total (Number): Order total amount
  - items (Map): For line items, contains product details and quantity
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Query by order_id returns all items in a single operation
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP3 (Get complete order details)
- **Capacity Planning**: Peak 8 RPS read, 3 RPS write - well within partition limits

### OrdersByUser GSI (on Orders table)

| user_id | order_date | order_id | status | total |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| user_123 | 2023-06-15T10:30:00Z | order_456 | DELIVERED | 129.99 |
| user_123 | 2023-05-20T14:22:00Z | order_442 | DELIVERED | 56.75 |

- **Purpose**: Enables querying orders by user with date-based sorting
- **Partition Key**: user_id - Groups all orders by user
- **Sort Key**: order_date - Enables date-based filtering and sorting
- **Projection**: INCLUDE (order_id, status, total) - Optimized for order history display
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP2 (List user's order history)
- **Capacity Planning**: Peak 5 RPS - well distributed across user_id values

### Products Table

| product_id | SK | name | description | price | category | inventory | image_url |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| prod_789 | DETAILS | Wireless Headphones | Bluetooth 5.0 over-ear headphones | 79.99 | Electronics | 45 | https://example.com/images/headphones.jpg |

- **Purpose**: Stores product catalog information
- **Aggregate Boundary**: Contains only product data
- **Partition Key**: product_id - Natural product identifier with high cardinality
- **Sort Key**: DETAILS - Constant value as this is a single-item table
- **Attributes**: 
  - name (String): Product name
  - description (String): Product description
  - price (Number): Current price
  - category (String): Product category
  - inventory (Number): Current stock level
  - image_url (String): Product image URL
- **Bounded Read Strategy**: Direct GetItem by product_id
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP6 (Get product details), AP7 (Check inventory)
- **Capacity Planning**: Peak 25 RPS read, 3 RPS write - well within partition limits

### ProductsByCategory GSI (on Products table)

| category | name | product_id | price | image_url |
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
| Electronics | Wireless Headphones | prod_789 | 79.99 | https://example.com/images/headphones.jpg |
| Electronics | Bluetooth Speaker | prod_790 | 49.99 | https://example.com/images/speaker.jpg |

- **Purpose**: Enables browsing products by category
- **Partition Key**: category - Groups products by category
- **Sort Key**: name - Enables alphabetical sorting within category
- **Projection**: INCLUDE (product_id, price, image_url) - Optimized for product listing
- **Access Patterns Served**: AP4 (Browse products by category)
- **Capacity Planning**: Peak 20 RPS - potential hot partition for popular categories

## Access Pattern Mapping

| Pattern | Description | Tables/Indexes | DynamoDB Operations | Implementation Notes |
|---------|-----------|---------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| AP1 | Get user profile by user ID | Users | GetItem(PK=user_id, SK=PROFILE) | Simple primary key lookup |
| AP2 | List user's order history | Orders (OrdersByUser GSI) | Query(PK=user_id, SK begins_with "2023") | Use SK for date range filtering |
| AP3 | Get complete order details | Orders | Query(PK=order_id) | Returns order metadata and all items |
| AP4 | Browse products by category | Products (ProductsByCategory GSI) | Query(PK=category) | Use Limit and LastEvaluatedKey for pagination |
| AP5 | Search products by name | - | - | Implement with OpenSearch integration |
| AP6 | Get product details | Products | GetItem(PK=product_id, SK=DETAILS) | Simple primary key lookup |
| AP7 | Check inventory levels | Products | GetItem(PK=product_id, ProjectionExpression=inventory) | Projected attribute for efficiency |
| AP8 | Create new user account | Users, EmailLookup | TransactWriteItems | Transaction ensures email uniqueness |
| AP9 | Update user profile | Users, EmailLookup | TransactWriteItems | Transaction if email changes |
| AP10 | Place new order | Orders, Products | TransactWriteItems | Transaction for order creation and inventory update |
| AP11 | Update order status | Orders | UpdateItem(PK=order_id, SK=METADATA) | Simple update operation |
| AP12 | Update product inventory | Products | UpdateItem with atomic counter | Use atomic counter for consistency |
| AP13 | Add new products | Products | PutItem | Simple put operation |
| AP14 | Update product details | Products | UpdateItem | Simple update operation |

## Hot Partition Analysis
- **Users Table**: Peak 10 RPS read across 1000 users = 0.01 RPS per partition ✅
- **Orders Table**: Peak 8 RPS read across thousands of orders = well distributed ✅
- **Products Table**: Peak 25 RPS read across product catalog = well distributed ✅
- **ProductsByCategory GSI**: Peak 20 RPS potentially concentrated on popular categories - **Mitigation**: Consider adding a random suffix for high-volume categories if needed

## Trade-offs and Optimizations

- **Aggregate Design**: Kept Orders and OrderItems together due to 95% access correlation - trades item size for query performance
- **Denormalization**: Duplicated basic product info (name, price) in OrderItems to avoid product lookups during order display - trades storage for performance
- **Normalization**: Kept Users as separate aggregate from Orders due to low access correlation (30%) - optimizes update costs
- **GSI Projection**: Used INCLUDE instead of ALL for OrdersByUser GSI to balance cost vs performance
- **External Search**: Recommended OpenSearch integration for product search by name/keywords rather than complex DynamoDB filtering

## Validation Results

- [x] Reasoned step-by-step through design decisions, applying DynamoDB design philosophy ✅
- [x] Aggregate boundaries clearly defined based on access pattern analysis ✅
- [x] Every access pattern solved or alternative provided ✅
